speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your specific symptoms and medical history, particularly regarding your delayed menstruation, any unusual physical features, or past fractures. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me your current age and whether you have experienced any spontaneous breaks in bones?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (likely 21-hydroxylase deficiency).

I have reviewed your history of delayed menarche, virilization (clitoromegaly, excessive hair growth), and bone fragility. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to see the results of your 17-hydroxyprogesterone level test. Please also confirm if you have any history of salt-wasting or hypotension as an infant.
